Recent findings suggest that the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam is an all-foam mattress that’s particularly suited to side sleepers and lightweight back sleepers. I slept on a Full size 10" mattress for a month, along with my husband, and I found it especially comfortable for side sleeping. I was also really impressed with the support it provided, considering its low price. But support at the edges left a lot to be desired and it won't be supportive enough for heavier sleepers, and my hot-sleeping husband found it slept way too warm, too.

Far more supportive than its price would suggest.

Temperature regulation isn’t great.

Not robust enough for stomach sleepers or those over 230lbs.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Insanely popular on Amazon, the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam Mattress is a cheap and cheerful all-foam offering that I freely admit I wasn’t expecting much from. However, there were lots of things about the Novilla Bliss that surprised me in a good way and overall, I was quite impressed by the support considering the mattress’ very reasonable pricing.

Name: Jo PlumridgeAge bracket: 45-55Weight bracket: 100-130lbsPredominant sleep position: Combination sleeper who spends slightly more time on her sideSleep problems: Suffers with back pain which can easily be exacerbated by an unsupportive mattress.

Industry observers note that it’s not going to rival the very best mattresses on the market but if you’re on a budget, this should definitely be on your radar. With a queen mattress right now priced at $269.99 in the Black Friday mattress deals, I think this is one of the best budget beds currently on the market.

In terms of firmness, I’d suggest that most sleepers will find it at the firmer end of the medium scale. There is sinkage and this is an all-foam mattress, but there’s still some support underneath. I can’t think of any other all-foam mattresses I’ve slept on that are as firm, except for the Nectar Classic Memory Foam. However, I must stress that I’m a lightweight sleeper and my husband, who is lightweight to average weight for a man, found it softer than I did.

In a recent development, still, we both enjoyed it for side sleeping particularly and, as someone who is ultra fussy about lumbar support, I found it more comfortable for back sleeping than I expected. Motion isolation on the Novilla Bliss is exceptional, and I couldn’t feel my husband moving around at all, but edge support is lacking both when you lie or sit on the edge. I didn’t feel as if I’d actually fall off the bed, but there was some definite tilting.

Type: Memory FoamFirmness: Medium (lighter sleepers will find it medium firm)Height: 10"Trial period: 100 nightsWarranty: 10 yearsPrice: From $179.99 at Novilla.

Sources indicate that the mattress' one significant failing, though, is temperature regulation. I sleep cold so this wasn't an concern, but my husband found it stuffy and, while he didn't wake up sweaty, he didn’t find it massively comfortable either. Hot sleepers on a budget might be happier on the Siena 10" Signature mattress, which kept our testers comfortably cool. But value for money is the Novilla Bliss' big selling point and considering its price, I was really impressed overall with the mattress.

Read on for my full assessment of the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam mattress so you can decide if it’s worth investing in.

Recent findings suggest that A queen size Novilla Bliss is listed at $269.99 with a 20% discount from $337.99 on the brand’s own website, while Amazon at the moment has the price at $269.99. This sale price seems to be fairly set, so here are the MSRPs for each size, plus the usual sale price you can expect to pay:.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

In a recent development, of course, November is one of the best times of the year for mattress sales and we’re seeing some Black Friday deals — a twin size Novilla 8" hybrid mattress is down to $90, for example, and on Amazon the queen size 10" Novilla Bliss has dropped below $210 a couple of times in 2026. So, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye on prices but do remember that, at $269.99 for a queen, the Novilla Bliss is already incredibly well priced.

Benefits differ very slightly depending on where you buy the mattress. On the brand’s own site, you’ll bet a 100-night trial, 10-year warranty and free shipping and returns. Amazon, on the other hand, offers a 90-night easy returns system, manufacturer’s warranty and free shipping and returns.

It has been revealed that an extremely affordable all-foam mattress that offers far more support than you’d expect for its price tag, a queen size Novilla Bliss is currently priced at $269.99 on both the brand’s own website and on Amazon. Keep an eye on prices as Black Friday approaches.

I tested the 10" version, but as detailed above, you can buy the Novilla Bliss in a variety of heights. But for this review, I’m concentrating on the middle ground of the 10” version. Starting at the top, there’s a breathable cover with OEKO-TEX certified fabric. This is helpfully removeable and washable — mattress covers that can’t be removed for freshening up are a real bugbear of mine, although I’d obviously recommend that you use a mattress protector anyway.

Underneath this is a layer of cooling memory foam that’s CertiPUR-US certified and contains the brand’s NanoGEL cooling particles, which Novilla notes are designed to ‘capture and redirect excess body heat away from the surface’.

It has been revealed that next up is a layer of adaptive cushioning foam that provides comfort and a transition layer to the high-density support foam layer underneath it. This layer provides most of the support and prevents the mattress from sagging.

Underneath this you’ll find the zip to remove the top cover, plus a non-slip fabric to stop the mattress from sliding about on your bed base. Somewhat annoyingly, the mattress doesn’t have handles to help move it about but as it’s all-foam, it’s not impossible to rotate it without them.

Industry observers note that as a lightweight sleeper, I rated the Novilla Bliss as a medium-firm mattress but my husband (and additional testers of a heavier build that I asked to try out the mattress) felt it was a medium, albeit a firmer medium. Averaging out scores, I’d probably place the mattress at a 6 out of 10 on the firmness scale.

There’s definitely some ‘squidge’ when you first lie on the mattress, but this is backed up by a decent amount of support from the lower levels. This combination makes it particularly suited for side sleepers. My husband in particular found the mattress instantly comfortable in this sleeping position, but it did take a couple of days for the foams to soften up a little at the shoulders for me — after this, it was extremely comfortable.

Pressure relief around the pressure points was also really good and I didn’t wake up with any symptoms of a dead hip (something that I can be prone to if the mattress is too unyielding).

Sources indicate that I wasn’t expecting great things from this mattress when it came to sleeping on my back, as I’ve historically found all-foam mattresses can lack the firmer lumbar support that I find essential. And, when I first lay down on the bed, I did notice a tiny amount of pulling through my lower back. However, this eased quickly and as a lightweight sleeper, I actually found the mattress supportive enough to keep my spine aligned.

Industry observers note that my husband, who boarders the lightweight and average weight category also found it pretty supportive. It’s not going to rival the very best mattresses for back pain but, overall, I thought it did an excellent job on pressure relief for both side and back sleeping.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re of a heavier weight though, I don’t think you’ll find the Novilla Bliss supportive enough and even average weight sleepers towards the higher end of that weight bracket may find it lacks support for back sleeping. I asked a couple of friends who are larger than my husband and I to try the mattress out and while they both thought they could just about get away with it for side sleeping, they felt that support was lacking for both back and stomach sleeping.

It has been revealed that in fact, strict stomach sleepers of any weight probably won’t get on with the Novilla Bliss as it’s just lacking in enough support to keep the hips lifted, leading to the spine sinking out of alignment. If you’re a stomach sleeper, have a look at our recommended mattresses for stomach sleepers instead.

Pressure relief score: 4 out of 5.

I’m in the UK so the mattress was shipped over the Atlantic and, despite its long journey, it arrived none the worse for its voyage. Order on the Novilla website and you’ll receive a tracking number within two business days, with delivery within three to seven business days. Novilla uses FedEx, UPS and GOFO Express for delivery. If you order through Amazon, you can expect delivery in around five days and there’s also the option to pay for the delivery drivers to unpack the mattress and take away packaging.

I recruited my long-suffering husband to help get the mattress upstairs although, being all-foam, it was considerably lighter than the hybrid and pocket sprung mattresses I’ve tested in the past.

In a recent development, once released from its vacuum seal, the Novilla Bliss did take longer than a hybrid mattress to inflate and I left it for a good 10 hours before sleeping on it. It did definitely continue to expand minutely over the next few days, so I’d say it was around 48 hours before it was fully expanded. The brand suggests that it will take 24-72 hours to fully expand, so this was bang on the money. Some Amazon customers have reported challenges with the mattress not expanding fully but in fairness, I didn’t have any issues on this front.

Like most foam mattresses, there was some off-gassing from the Novilla Bliss. It wasn’t the worst I’ve come across but it did last for a couple of days.

Delivery and setup score: 4 out of 5.

In a recent development, my husband and I slept on the mattress for four weeks to get a clear overview of how it performed in key areas. In addition, I carried out some objective tests in an approximation of our comprehensive sleep lab testing methodology.

Sources indicate that through both objective and subjective testing, I’ve assessed the mattress in three key areas. I’ve looked at motion isolation (will a partner moving about at night disturb you?), temperature regulation (does the mattress keep a hot sleeper comfortable through the night?) and edge support (how solid does the edge of the bed feel when you lie right on it or sit on the mattress?). These are the results.

If you share your bed with a restless partner or are a light sleeper, a mattress with good motion isolation is a must. Good motion isolation stops movement from one side of the bed travelling over and waking up another sleeper. I can report back that the Novilla Bliss is particularly strong in this department.

In a recent development, my husband does tend to flail about in bed when he’s rolling over, channeling a walrus trying to leave the ocean and I’m a pretty light sleeper, so even a little motion transfer can be enough to wake me up. I’m pleased to report that I wasn’t disturbed by him at all during our testing period, which was an unusual and pleasing thing.

This was backed up by my objective tests. Firstly, I performed a series of drop tests. I placed a wine glass on the left-hand side of the mattress and dropped a weight from 24" above the bed surface on the right-hand side. This is a similar sensation to a person getting into bed.

It has been revealed that I dropped the weight five times consecutively 30" away from the wine glass. Each time, the wine glass gave a very slight wobble but otherwise stayed upright, which was impressive. Next up, I got my husband to perform some subjective tests, starting with low force movements and then increasing to moderate and high force movements. I rated the mattress 10 out of 10 at low force and nine out of 10 at both moderate and high force. Overall, the Novilla Bliss really excelled when it came to motion isolation.

It has been revealed that when I talk about temperature regulation, I’m looking at how well the mattress manages heat build-up throughout the night and whether it leaves a sleeper feeling stuffy. I’m afraid this was one area where the Novilla Bliss didn’t perform brilliantly, despite claims of a breathable cover and gel-infused memory foam.

Sources indicate that my husband sleeps hot and he found the mattress stuffy after only 15 minutes of lying on it. And while he didn’t wake up seriously overheating, he did feel slightly clammy and uncomfortable. It was not a particularly breathable mattress and, on some hotter nights during testing, he did actually decamp to our spare room.

Industry observers note that I’m something of a reptile at the best of times but even I noticed some heat building up around my lower back while lying on it. However, thanks to my cold nature, I wasn’t ever uncomfortable on it.

We tested through the tail end of an unusually warm period in the UK and through to some slightly cooler nights, so it gave me a good overall view of the mattress. For context, temperatures in the room ranged from around 75F down to 60F. However, I should point out that I wouldn’t expect an all-foam mattress to perform as well as a hybrid for temperature regulation and, if you are a hot sleeper, you’d be better off investing in one of our best cooling mattress picks.

Temperature control: 2.5 out of 5.

Industry observers note that A mattress with good edge support allows sleepers to use the whole width of the bed, as well as providing a stable surface to sit on while getting in and out of bed. My husband and I foster cats for a local charity and, as any cat servant will tell you, these little furry creatures have the ability to take up 90% of the bed overnight, leaving human subjects very much clinging to the edges.

In a recent development, unfortunately, the Novilla Bliss wasn’t the strongest candidate when it came to edge support. There was some definite tilting when we lay on the edges, although I didn’t feel as if I’d actually fall off. It was a similar story when sitting on the edge of the bed — there was some definite tilting, but I didn’t feel as if I’d actually slip off.

Sources indicate that to back up my experiences, I placed a 53lb weight midway across and 3" in from the foot and sides of the mattress. The weight sunk in by 5" immediately and dropped further to 6.5" after five minutes. And I had to get my husband to hold the weight the whole time (he only took his hands off very briefly for a photograph).

I repeated this test midway down and 3" in from the side of the mattress and got exactly the same results, with the weight needing to be held the whole time. Just for context, the same weight placed in the center of the mattress compressed by 5" immediately but then didn’t drop any further.

The Novilla Bliss receives overwhelmingly positive reviews from sleepers on both Amazon and the brand’s website. There’s lots of praise for the “exceptional” price and many sleepers praise it for its good quality. Sleepers also praise the mattress for pressure relief, with one customer describing it as the “perfect balance of softness and support…I woke up feeling much more rested without the usual aches and stiffness.” Overall, this is a recurrent theme, along with frequent praise for the motion isolation.

There are nearly 45,000 reviews for the mattress on Amazon so, as you might expect, you will find some complaints in there. The most common one seems to be poor expansion of the mattress, so it would seem that this might be something you’ll need to look out for. And, while many people praise the mattress for soothing aches and pains, stomach sleepers and those of a heavier build complain that the mattress is nowhere near supportive enough for their sleeping style or body weight.

✅ You’re a side sleeper of light or average weight: The Novilla Bliss excelled in pressure relief and comfort for side sleepers, easing tension and providing enough support for a really comfortable night’s sleep.

✅ You share your bed with a restless partner: There really wasn’t any motion transfer to speak of with the Novilla Bliss and I never felt disturbed by my husband moving about.✅ You’re on a budget: At $269.99 for a queen size, the Novilla Bliss is exceptionally good value for money and holds its own against some more expensive options.

According to recent reports, ❌You sleep on your stomach or are of a heavier build: The all-foam construction of the Novilla Bliss simply isn’t supportive enough for stomach sleepers or those who weigh over 230lbs. Try the Siena Signature mattress instead if you’re on a budget and fall into these categories.❌You’re a hot sleeper: The Novilla Bliss left my hot-sleeping husband feeling pretty stuffy and uncomfortable and its all-foam construction does trap heat a little too easily. The SweetNight CoolNest Memory Foam mattress offers excellent temperature regulation and is another budget option. ❌You need excellent edge support: The Novilla Bliss suffered with some sinkage at its edges and didn’t feel like the most secure surface to lie on the edge of or sit on. If you need an affordable mattress with decent edge support, check out the EGOHOME Black 12” Memory Foam mattress instead.

Recent findings suggest that there are plenty of positives about the Novilla Bliss, but the price is the overwhelming winner. At under $300 for a queen, it’s a bit of a bargain and I was impressed by how well it performed considering that price tag. It certainly beats out quite a few more expensive mattresses when it comes to side sleeping in particular. The soft foams at the top and some decent support underneath mean that this is a great option for side sleepers, except for those of a heavier weight.

In a recent development, it also boasts some of the best motion isolation I’ve come across, and it will be a winner for co-sleepers thanks to this. But, as mentioned, I don’t think it’s a great fit for hot sleepers and I would like to see better edge support.

But overall, I was hugely impressed with this mattress, and I think that most lightweight and average side and back sleepers will be comfortable on this mattress.

This plush pillow is available in two sizes and two different firmness options. In our SquishPillow review, our tester found it best suited to side sleepers, which will match well with the Novilla Bliss. It's also only $29.99, so a bit of a bargain.

Rated the best bed sheets for hot sleepers by our bedding testers, these sheets are silky-soft and cool-to-touch — so they could help to make the Novilla Bliss a bit cooler to sleep on. And there are over a dozen colors/patterns to choose from.

Sources indicate that another way to help make a mattress cooler is to add a cooling mattress topper. The Lucid Gel Memory Foam mattress topper did a great job of keeping our tester cool and it's reasonably priced for such a nice thick topper. A thinner and cheaper 2" version could also save you some money.

When natural light isn't available, the best sunrise alarm clocks are the next best thing. You won't get a better gadget than the Hatch Restore 3 for this and, although it's not the cheapest purchase, it could really help to keep you happy through the winter months.

The best cheap option in our best weighted blankets round up, the YNM Original Cotton Weighted Blanket has a significant choice of weights and lots of different colours to choose from - many of which are often dramatically reduced on Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

According to recent reports, it was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a latest character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active users to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

"Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

It has been revealed that looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be confirmed, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart fresh additions build on what made the original work so well.

#28658. Breaking: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that at this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed.
  • A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite.
  • Recent findings suggest that you likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

Recent findings suggest that you likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

Almost nothing here works, figuratively and literally. Within three minutes of the opening mission, before Madsen's undercover cop Tanner goes undercover, you're ordered to join some marked police cars to head for a bust – but because the rozzers' primary function is to give chase to you, later on, driving too close crosses their wires, provoking them into blue-on-blue ramming maneuvres. Later, in a motorbike sprint down an inexplicably exploding beach, cartel goons are positioned across the sand, presumably to take drama-enhancing pot shots. They're so slow, however, both to notice your presence and to physically raise their guns, that they're barely out of their idle animations by the time you whizz past. And your own guy isn't much better: an assassination mission, which ends with your target cornered from an elevated position, requires that you take a few steps backwards first, as Tanner can't drop his shootin' arms low enough to land a hit from the balcony he's on.

Unlike Vice City's Tommy Vercetti, he can at least swim, which by 2004 standards gives the seaside Miami and Nice maps a fair verisimilitude, particularly when a shot-up boat engine forces the abandoning of ship. No amount of product-of-its-time concessions, though, can account for how woodenly unpalatable the on-foot action is. Controls are stiff and shooting feels meaningless, with zero tangible sense of bullets being sent nor received; killing a man carries all the weight of just shouting at him to lie down, and if it weren't for sound effects and the dwindling health bar, I could park Tanner in front of a firing squad of identically-modelled thugs with almost zero impression that his lungs were filling with Uzi rounds.

In a recent development, driver, of course, began as a pure wheelman sim, later installments only letting you hoof it after someone at developers Reflections began smelling that Rockstar money. It was therefore always unlikely, even for the purported GTA killer, that this would achieve action-adventure sophistication in its bipedal bits. Even so, god, it's woeful. Stingy checkpointing also means that failure is often punished by having to replay those tedious, flavourless shootouts in full.

Recent findings suggest that the driving is better, which is a bit like saying there's decent cheese in this cheese and smallpox toastie. It's reasonably slidey, when throwing the back end through a curving French alleyway, and in contrast to the gunplay, there is a somewhat realised tactility to ploughing around in two tonnes of rolling metal. It has problems of its own, mind. Cars feel okay when they're moving, but contact and crashes are leaden, sluggish, visually underwhelming occasions that I would call non-events, were they not so slow to recover from that a single nasty impact can scupper a timed mission. Granted, I promptly re-learned how vital it is to keep both eyes on the road, as other vehicles, pedestrians, lamposts, and other detritus tend to pop into existence some mere fifty feet in front of my speeding bumper.

Recent findings suggest that the result, of both this graphical shortcoming and the overly punishing crashes, is a getaway car sim that too often encourages you to drive like cataract-ridden grandparent. Worse, whoever put Letty Ortiz in a lunchbox must have also been in charge of the engine noises, producing an array of miserable high-rev dins – especially for the motorbikes, which screech like amateurishly autotuned vacuum cleaners. There are also shades of that deranged cop AI in ordinary commuters, who I've repeatedly seen swerving and slaloming around empty lanes, seemingly for no reason beyond violent confusion.

Recent findings suggest that strangely enough, my 2026 return has largely dodged the game's infamous glitchiness, the worst instance of physics defiance being a garage door that appeared to lift Tanner into the air before propelling him, incorporeally, through the car shed's roof. I recall much worse, from the days when I'd have my dad rent it for me from Blockbuster. Mission-critical NPCs getting stuck on walls; flipped pursuit cars spinning endlessly; getting flung into space when walking on an overturned vehicle (a common occurrence, given the actual 'crawling out' animation sometimes failed to play, the game instead teleporting you onto the spring-loaded underside instead).

I've thus far escaped these, but as far as I know, they're still lurking dormant, and none of what I've witnessed with adult eyes has been funny or stupid enough to imbue Driv3r 3 The Third with a Wiseauean so-bad-it's-good quality. It's just bad. It was always bad. Why did I even entertain the possibility that it wasn't bad?

Reflections, to their credit, accepted their folly. Narratively unrelated sequel Driver: Parallel Lines tucked away a bin full of discarded copies, at least until Ubisoft bought up the series and patched it out, and for all the fantastical coma silliness of direct followup Driver: San Francisco, that was sensible enough to keep Tanner where he best belongs: hands on the wheel, foot on the gas, gun holstered. And was a far, far better game for it, too.

As 2011's San Francisco launch also remains the most recent Driver release, I regretfully can't end with the assurance that DrIIIver's legacy is a mere blip on a redeemed franchise. That stain stank, and did for ages, very possibly to the extent that GTA's one-time biggest rival never recovered.

Still, even if Reflections couldn't fully turn around their fortunes, the consistent improvement from this to Parallel Lines to San Francisco highlighted that they did learn something. Maybe so too did anyone else who went on to make an open-world action game. Which wouldn't be the worst outcome; after all, those who do not learn from gnarled, stinking wrecks like this are doomed to repeat them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that openAI has recently reported that its frontier models attempted to rewrite AMD circuits and received an up-to 14% PPA (Power, Performance and Area) boost. OpenAI states these rewrites are "production-viable" too (via BigGo Finance).

The claim is not that humans couldn't make these same optimisations, but instead that it did around a year's worth of design optimisations in less than 5 months, an optimisation of optimisation, if you will. (Okay, I'll stop writing optimisation now.).

Apparently, AMD has even incorporated some of these findings into chip designs that have recently gone to manufacturing. The model worked on an in-house "Jalapeño" chip, as well as an AMD "flagship GPU IP" and "AMD next-gen flagship CPU key modules." Each one of these saw different gains.

It has been revealed that for the Jalapeño vector compute unit, the model's changes managed to reduce cell area by around 13%, and this was observed when powering on the hardware. The Jalapeño compute unit saw the standard cell area reduced by around 10%, with the multiplier area alone reduced by around 15 % and latency cut from two clock cycles to one.

It's the AMD flagship GPU that saw the 14% PPA improvement, and AMD has reportedly verified a 'single-digit' PPA improvement on the next-gen CPU.

Recent findings suggest that using a budget of around 112,000 tokens, all models in the report (GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-5.6 Sol) performed better when asked to design a RISC-V core from scratch, rather than optimising one given to them. That being noted, OpenAI does note that models asked to entirely redesign rather than optimise could omit features in the original design, which can become its own problem.

Generative AI is a bit of a double-edged sword in the PC hardware space. Before mentioning the memory crisis the AI global buildout is responsible for, generative AI's ability to work constantly and fast can be a boon for development, but it can also be a slog to work through. Linux engineers are at the moment struggling to get on top of the thousands of bugs AI is finding, which is a real monkey's paw element of the tech. And it's a sign that AI itself needs to be maintained and monitored, even if it genuinely does seem to produce favourable results in engineering.

Feature: GTA 6 Made Me Want to Be a Good Guy (or Girl)

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.
  • I’m playing a upcoming GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.
  • I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.

I’m playing a upcoming GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.

The more I reflect on my time with GTA 6, the more I realise this is not the GTA I necessarily grew up with, even though the carnage is always there bubbling beneath the surface.

That’s because just like GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, I do have the option to go on a reckless murdering spree.

I could stock up on grenades and sticky bombs and create chaos on a highway.

I could go to a beach and mow down innocent bystanders in a scene so gruesome it’d make Jack Thompson pass out.

I think this is the most remarkable thing about GTA 6 – it’s made me play differently to past titles, even though nothing has actually changed.

In a recent development, so, why is this? Why am I choosing non-lethal as much as humanly possible, when the game allows me to go mental if I want to?

I think it’s a few reasons, personally.

Firstly, Jason and Lucia certainly aren’t saints by any stretch, but they just don’t seem like the type to go on a killing spree.

This isn’t the first GTA game to have protagonists with a slightly softer personality – GTA 4’s Niko immediately springs to mind, as does GTA 5’s Franklin.

But I think with romance being one of this game’s central themes, you really get to know these characters intimately.

It’s about the quiet moments, rubbing your partner’s feet in front of the TV.

It’s relatable – and if it’s relatable, then I think the vast, vast, vast majority of us are kind and caring to others.

Of course, this is still a video game and I racked up kills in the hundreds by the end of the campaign, but I never felt like I was doing it on purpose.

According to recent reports, I made mistakes – I sometimes knocked cyclists clean into the air. I wouldn’t do that in real-life. But I did try to avoid these moments as much as possible here.

One other wrinkle is that the realistic graphics mean the violence is pretty visceral. It’s fascinating to think how much criticism the PS2 trilogy got at the time, when it looks like a cartoon compared to this game.

I wouldn’t say the violence necessarily deterred me from being a cold-blooded killer, but I can see how it would affect others.

And also it’s a gameplay mechanic, right?

Behaving recklessly and showing no real care for other virtual life will alter your criminal profile, and change how the world reacts to you.

I ended up with a personality trait sitting somewhere between saint and sinner, but I think that’s probably normal as you’re still going to have to punch an NPC in the mouth from time-to-time.

I’m sure there’ll be people who see the GTA series as more of an arcade game than the life sim it’s become in GTA 6, and there’ll be many who don’t like this change.

In a recent development, for me, I’m fascinated by how Rockstar subtly convinced me to play a GTA game like it’s not a GTA game. And I didn’t even really notice it until recently.

That’s just one of the title’s many, many achievements – and one of the reasons why it’s now the highest rated game of all time.

Have you found you’re playing GTA 6 in a less aggressive manner than past titles? Are you taking care on the road and picking the non-lethal option wherever possible? Be a bit nicer to the Leonida natives in the comments section below.

#28654. Industry News: The Story Behind Gibbs' Head Slap On NCIS Hilariously Involves Michael Weatherly

Industry News: The Story Behind Gibbs' Head Slap On NCIS Hilariously Involves Michael Weatherly

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For years, Leroy Jethro Gibbs was the face of NCIS.
  • Mark Harmon spoke on its origins in an interview with Cheat Sheet, and how a bit of improvisation became an iconic recurring bit.
  • Michael is a hugely talented actor, as is every member of this cast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For years, Leroy Jethro Gibbs was the face of NCIS. His litany of rules and quirks was the heart and soul of the series, with his trademark head slap being one of them. As he's back in primetime on the Origins spinoff, I'm learning the slap all started with his former co-star, Michael Weatherly.

Mark Harmon spoke on its origins in an interview with Cheat Sheet, and how a bit of improvisation became an iconic recurring bit. Harmon set the scene far back before the 2026 TV schedule, all the way back to the first year of the series:.

Michael is a hugely talented actor, as is every member of this cast. My memory of when that happened, we were doing a scene. And he was on a Navy ship and he was talking to a female petty officer. I think this was in year one, early. And he was doing what he does, which is sometimes stay on script and sometimes not. I just reached over and smacked him. I tried to put him back on line. It was an instinct. It wasn’t thought, I didn’t think about it, I just did it.

It has been revealed that funny to think this all started partly because Mark Harmon was frustrated with Michael Weatherly going off script. I could imagine filming days were long enough without improvisation that it could sabotage a scene that was perfectly written as-is. I can empathize with Harmon just wanting to move on, and giving Weatherly a smack on the head to remind him that other people would like to move on as well.

According to recent reports, in fairness to Weatherly, Harmon's head slap could've caused a much bigger distraction had he completely broken character and gotten into a fight with his co-star. Fortunately, Harmon confirmed the Tony DiNozzo actor didn't miss a beat, and it became a part of the show's history:.

It has been revealed that to his credit, he stayed in the scene; he didn’t break. And I didn’t break. And the girl in the scene playing the petty officer, she was shocked, she was surprised. And she stayed there, and we just kept going. And people liked it. And every episode I was smacking him–maybe too much. We still do that occasionally, but sparingly. That’s where it came from.

It may not be the sole reason that NCIS is now a franchise generating billions of dollars across its lifetime, but it certainly contributed. Tony and Gibbs' relationship was one of the show's best parts in its early years, and many still remember it fondly.

What's funny about this story is that Michael Weatherly largely remembers it the same way, but added on detail that Harmon left out. In the moment, no one knew that the head smack was going to be something iconic in NCIS. It was only Season 1, and they were just a few episodes in.

Instead, Weatherly only remembers that he was goofing off, and everyone on set was mad at him afterward for potentially ruining a shot. It wasn't until they saw the head smack in the editing room that producers liked it and decided to make it a part of the episode and the show.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that these days, Weatherly's Tony doesn't get a ton of head smacks. He's currently the acting director of the NCIS team, and also occasionally jumping in to lend a hand in investigations. I don't imagine anyone wants to slap the boss man on the back of the head, but I'd be up for seeing someone try.

Recent findings suggest that the main features of the free 'Florin' update are outlined by Paradox in the video above, and unless you're really into the nitty gritty details of realm and wealth management, there's one bit of it which stands out. The option to play as a landless adventurer has finally made its way into the base game, as Paradox promised earlier this year.

This means you can kick off a playthrough as a lowborn leader of a travelling band or a wandering noble with claims on realms ruled by others. Originally locked behind the Roads to Power DLC, the option to start off this way or end up living if you end up deposed from your throne of choice is a great addition to the story arc of any CK3 run. No longer are you glued to the throne from day one to the day you quit for good - power's a privilege which can be earned and revoked depending on what you get up to. Though, it's worth noting that only three ways of operating as a landless adventurer are being made free to access with this update. You can be an aimless wanderers, sword-toting mercenaries, or scholars. If you want your band to earn their living as explorers, free booters, or legitimists, you'll still need Roads to Power.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty major bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

Recent findings suggest that "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

Sources indicate that "One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV reveals and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Take-Two Interactive, the parent firm of Rockstar Games, has published GTA 6's day-one retail sales, and they're predictably astronomical and record-breaking.

Via BusinessWire, Rockstar and Take-Two announce that GTA 6's launch day sales, based on estimates through end of day on November 19, reached $3.79 billion, surpassing any other launch across all entertainment mediums and officially making GTA 6 the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

The companies also reveal that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies pre-release, which is another "upcoming record across all platforms." For comparison, 2022 Game of the Year Elden Ring sold 30 million copies in three years.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a upcoming chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," says Rockstar co-founder and GTA veteran Sam Houser. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Even though the industry has been anticipating GTA 6 to be the biggest game of all time, and very possibly the biggest entertainment product ever, for a while now based on the game's estimated budget of $1-1.5 billion, seeing these numbers become official is staggering.

Elden Ring was a massively successful game when it released back in 2022, and seeing its near-lifetime sales be eclipsed by GTA 6 in a single day is truly astounding no matter how inevitable Rockstar's success has always seemed.

As digital-only GTA 6 smashes records, GameStop CEO notes move from physical copies "has hurt consumers" as they "should be able to sell" or trade purchases.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back.
  • "Prior to the Tech giant's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the company created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the company's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Tech giant's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

According to recent reports, this tallies with the narrative spun by co-manufacturer leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

In a recent development, the situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "massive American tech giant" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

It had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it launched, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

It has been revealed that build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was declared in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

It has been revealed that per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole upcoming "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens". I need somebody to authenticate whether this is a truthful statement, or developer TinyToad pulling a fast one. In the meantime, I'll say that 1) I have now managed to kill several ogres, 2) I like Korridor's electro-metal soundtrack.

In Korridor, you're a bald medieval monk garbed in Poundshop Adeptus Astartes platemail. You've woken up in a dungeon of mysterious provenance, and must walk very slowly down its corridors korridors while shooting and punching goblins, wraiths and demons hurrying the other way. Each enemy has a numerical health indicator, and the basic challenge is working out whether you can empty it before they walk into you – which costs you a proportionate amount of health, mitigated by armour. As you go, you'll walk through a choice of gates that grant buffs such as faster health regen, bullet penetration, or nippier horizontal motion.

The fact that you don't control how fast the monk trudges vertically allows the game to synch the onslaught pretty tightly to the thudding, growling score. It reminds me a little of Thumper, though it isn't nearly so invigoratingly malevolent. So far. At intervals, the beat thickens and all the enemies burst into a sprint, throwing their arms up and conveying the strong impression that they are more running away from something than running at you. There's clearly a dreadful entity at the far end of the dungeon. Perhaps it is another overdressed monk with an even bigger gun.

Industry observers note that is this how those mobile games actually work? If it is, then alas and alack, all is lost. I've finally succumbed to those adverts, and all it took was some disingenuous Steam copy promising to place them at a critical remove. Curse you, TinyToad. Curse you and your gates. If you were actually a toad, I'd step on you. Still, now that we've broken the ice, can you please make another game in which I get to play one of those gloating giantesses in Hero Wars? Because I know some people who dig that kind of thing.

Publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have confirmed Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Recent findings suggest that saihate Station first debuted for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:.

Since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”.

Haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

Then, the truth of the world closes in.

Recent findings suggest that the main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

Industry observers note that starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I think we all knew it was going to be big, but this big? Rockstar has declared that GTA 6 sold a staggering 32.5 million copies during its preload period, setting a “upcoming record across all platforms”.

That number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful. (It’s only going to keep rising through Thanksgiving and Christmas, too.).

Rockstar says the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Estimates claim it cost about $1 billion to make.

It’s also eager to point out that the title is now the highest-rated game of all-time as well, with its near-perfect 99 Metacritic score nudging the N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time aside.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a latest chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of GTA 6. We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”.

The dev didn’t specify how sales were split between systems, but the expectation is the PS5 version sold best, with some estimates pegging it at around 75% of the total.

Sony was the primary marketing partner of the game, and promoted the fact it “plays best on PS5” (even though testing shows it’s broadly identical to the Xbox Series X version on base hardware).

This is just the beginning for GTA 6, of course, with no word on Rockstar’s aims for the next iteration of GTA Online just yet. The game is also expected to launch on PC in 2027 as well.

If you’re one of the 32.5 million people playing, don’t forget to check out our GTA 6 guide for tons of information on the game.

Infinity Nikki fans threaten to boycott game after promotion by Elon Musk's mother, but there may be a genuine reason for her involvement

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates.
  • According to recent reports, some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk.
  • While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

According to recent reports, some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a upcoming upgrade - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear.".

"If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong.".

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

"She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY.".

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese organization makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

Recent findings suggest that so far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

According to recent reports, the Hunger Games movies have entertained audiences for decades now, and we're getting yet another book to screen adaptation with Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping. The latest prequel tells the story of Haymitch's games, with actor Joseph Zada perfectly emulating Woody Harrelson. There are still some surprises for those who read the book, including a few references to Lucy Gray from Songbirds and Snakes (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) that weren't in the source material. CinemaBlend spoke to the movie's director about why those changes were made for the latest installment in the franchise.

Industry observers note that years after the original Hunger Games movies, we've returned to Panem thanks to author Suzanne Collins' pair of prequels. First was Songbirds and Snakes, which followed a young President Snow who fell in love with and then lost Rachel Zegler's Lucy Gray Baird. Lucy Gray's fate is left ambiguous in both the film and book, as she disappeared and fled from Snow after winning the 10th Hunger Games.

Recent findings suggest that sunrise on the Reaping's movie deviates from the book by having Snow mention Lucy Gray by name when talking to Haymitch at Plutarch's home. As you can see in the video above, I had to ask Francis Lawrence about this change, and he told me:.

That's not in the book. And that came out of conversations that we had with Suzanne and our screenwriter when we're going through and just talking about, you know, you have to go into every scene and go 'How? Why?' all of that. And we started to question about Snow making this appearance and why him coming in person is so important, especially when he's, you know, not feeling so well. Not to spoil anything. And that's what we came up with, which I was really happy about is this idea of this kind of personal quest that for 40 years he's still been obsessed with what happened to Lucy Gray.

In a recent development, honestly, this makes a great deal of sense. While Haymitch makes a quick enemy out of Snow during the Chariot sequence that killed Louella, why would the President of Panem (played in this film by Ralph Fiennes) show up in person to intimidate him? This scene was expanded in the film by having Snow specifically talk about Lucy Gray, the District 12 victor and his love interest that he's still seemingly searching for. Whether or not we ever get confirmation about her ultimate fate remains to be seen.

In addition to Snow name-dropping Lucy Gray, we also get another reference to Zegler's character during the funeral scene towards the end of the movie. At the services for the District 12 tributes like Maysilee, the Covey sing "The Old Therebefore," the song Lucy Gray belts out as snakes cover her body at the end of her Games. In our same conversation Lawrence explained how this came about, telling me:.

Suzanne is a real music aficionado. And, you know, she obviously was very involved in writing many lyrics for the previous songs and all of that. And has, you know, sort of her mythology of how these songs have been sung and what songs have been passed along. That was one of the ideas too, is that that's the kind of song that you would sing at a funeral, which is partially why Lucy Gray sings it when she thinks that she's gonna die, so that she's almost singing her own funeral song. So, but it's just nice that you, you feel those kind of connections, and it's the same with The Hanging Tree, you hear Lucy Gray singing that, but you've already heard Katniss singing it.

Sources indicate that I honestly love this attention to detail. While these are not huge moments in the Hunger Games movies, the way songs are used throughout the franchise helps to make the cinematic universe feel more interconnected. There's a ton of lore within the story of Panem, and these small changes to Sunrise on the Reaping will no doubt be powerful for longtime fans of the YA franchise.

Sunrise on the Reaping's reviews have been mixed, but now moviegoing audiences will get to judge the latest Hunger Games flick for themselves. Fans are hoping to see more prequels in the future, but that'll presumably only happen once Suzanne Collins release another novel. Fingers crossed that happens sooner rather than later.

Latest Update: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them.
  • Sources indicate that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress.
  • It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

Sources indicate that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a fresh manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a major heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," states David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style.".

That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," notes Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to New Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.
